text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia is very serious about the return of Serbs and does not question the issue. However the return should not be improvised but organised, says Foreign Minister Mate Granic.
- A mysterious tunnel discovered two days ago under the divided city of Mostar might have served as an underground passage for Moslem sabotage units during the Moslem-Croat war in Bosnia.

- Head of the Dominican order Marinko Zadro has sent a fraternal warning or 'correctio fraterna' to Vjekoslav Lasic, a priest who has publicly glorified Croatia's World War Two fascist leader Ante Pavelic.
- Bosnian Croat refugees now living in the formerly Serb-held Krajina region around the town of Plaski say they are constantly provoked by returning Serbs.
- The opposition is unlikely to have a joint candidate for the presidential elections since the Social Democrats decided to put forward their own candidate, Zdravko Tomac.

- Croatian power board (HEP) started disconnecting companies, including Rijeka port, which owe it money for electricity. Its uncollected debts from customers directly connected to the grid total 1.12 billion kuna.

- A Dubrovnik American College of Management and Technology will open its doors to students in September with a two-year course in tourism and management. The annual fee is put at $2,500 for full-time and at $5,000 for part-time students.

- Banking news: Private Partner Banka opened its fourth office in Zagreb on Wednesday which will now serve as its headquarters. The bank ended 1996 with 13.5 million kuna profit and total assets of 226.5 million kuna.
- Some 645,000 Yugoslav dinars have so far been converted into kuna in the two main towns of Eastern Slavonia, says Josip Malkoc, head of Vukovar's central payments bureau (ZAP).

- Editorial: Croatia has come under strong pressure to allow mass return of Serbs. But international diplomacy does not insist on reciprocal return of refugees to Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia which brings Zagreb into an unfavourable position.

- Two councillors of Croatian Peasant Party (HSS) who voted for the ruling HDZ party in the Zagreb city assembly and were later suspended by their party leadership say they asked the HDZ for nothing in return.
- Five brokerages out of 47 that are members of the Zagreb bourse are owned by foreigners. The bourse now charges 300,000 kuna for a permanent member slot.
- Former Zagreb city council president Zdravko Tomac demands suspension from the council of the HSS members who voted for the HDZ mayor.
- Australian Croats say they are ready to vote in Croatian presidential elections.
- Dairies question profitability of cheese production in the face of cheaper imports from Bosnia and even Germany. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
